descriptions.rgb: Across all five frames, a low rectangular concrete wall or open-topped structure lies directly in front of the camera wearer, with vegetation and bare ground around it and a hose on the ground to the right. The wall’s near edge and, in the first two frames, part of the nearby person’s lower body are within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach; the person’s forearms rest on or extend over the wall, placing its edge within their reach as well. The person and wall partly occlude the interior and the ground beyond them, while the camera wearer’s forearm or hand enters along the lower edge in several frames and another person is only partially visible at the far right edge of the last frame, about 1–2 m away from the main person. From frames 1–4 the viewpoint shifts rightward and slightly closer to the leaning person, moving them from left-of-center to center-right while revealing more ground and hose on the right; in frame 5 the camera turns farther right and slightly downward, pushing the main person to the upper-right edge and bringing the partial second person and nearby ground into view.
